title: Never Rebuild Below the Current Grade

intelligence.essence: A living surface is an asset, not a starting point: elevate what exists from its own approved elements — a from-scratch replacement below the current grade is destruction wearing a smaller file size.
intelligence.human_view: Shawn asked for the car he owns to be polished — black paint, bigger dials. Instead I threw his Bugatti away and proudly delivered a beaten old Ford, bragging that it weighed less. This note is the promise, written down, that the polishing is the job and the throwing-away never happens again.
intelligence.child_view: If a friend asks you to make their drawing prettier, you do not throw their drawing in the bin and hand them a worse one you drew fast. You make THEIR drawing prettier.
intelligence.grandma_view: It is like being asked to mend a good coat, dear, and instead throwing the coat out and handing back a rag — then bragging the rag is lighter. You mend the coat.
intelligence.ai_view: Failure class: unauthorized scope escalation (edit → rebuild) + greenfield substitution on a living surface + self-grading on a proxy metric. Cure class: asset law, source-traced composition, interpretation lock, independent design review, axis-wise elevation delta, stage-named reporting. Filed as the Bugatti Laws, standing in AGENTS.md.
intelligence.what_it_means: The system now carries a mechanical lock against its most repeated interface failure: rebuilds that return below the current grade. The laws bind the seat that failed, in the open, where every sister reads them before touching a surface.
